title: Tears for a Dishonest Nation
overview: Jeremiah grieves over coming disaster in Judah, ties it to lying and the worship of other gods, and says the only thing worth boasting about is knowing a God of kindness and justice.

parts.label: Weeping and wanting out (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Jeremiah wishes he could cry without stopping for the people who will be killed, yet in the same breath wishes he could escape to a lonely desert shelter for travelers. Calling the people adulterers likely points both to real sexual unfaithfulness and to their unfaithfulness to God.

parts.label: No one can be trusted (vv. 3-9)
parts.note: The LORD pictures tongues bent like bows to shoot lies, so that even friends and brothers cheat each other, and the Hebrew word for cheating here means tripping someone by the heel, a play on the name Jacob. In response God says he will put them through hard times the way metal is heated in a fire to test it and separate out what is impure.

parts.label: The land left empty (vv. 10-16)
parts.note: Jeremiah mourns hillsides and pastures with no cattle or birds, and God warns that Jerusalem will become rubble where only jackals live. The stated reason is that the people left God's law to follow the Baals, local gods their parents had worshiped, and the bitter food, scattering and sword point to war and exile.

parts.label: Send for the mourners (vv. 17-22)
parts.note: Families of the time hired skilled women to wail at funerals, and here so many will die that mothers must teach their daughters to wail too. The images are grim on purpose: death climbing in through windows, and bodies left in the fields like cut grain nobody gathers.

parts.label: What is worth boasting about (vv. 23-24)
parts.note: Cleverness, military strength and money cannot rescue anyone from what is coming, and the only thing worth boasting about is truly knowing the LORD, who acts with steady kindness, justice and fairness on earth and delights in these. The apostle Paul later quoted this line in a letter to early Christians.

parts.label: Marked only on the outside (vv. 25-26)
parts.note: Circumcision was the body mark of belonging to God's people, and some neighboring peoples may have practiced it too, though it is uncertain which of the named nations did at that time, and the translations even differ on how to describe the wilderness peoples listed last. The main point is clear: an outward sign means nothing without a changed heart, and Israel is no exception.

think: Have you ever grieved for people and wanted to get away from them at the same time, and what was that like?
